utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are Friday and I would like to greet all the people in the courtroom. I should like to greet the Prosecution. Ms. Dahl in particular, Mr. Seselj, as well as all the people who are assisting us today for this Status Conference. First of all, this Status Conference will be held until 7.00 p.m., but if we are not able to address all the items on the agenda, I have every intention of pursuing the matter on Monday afternoon. I don't know whether Mr. Seselj is -- has any visits on Monday afternoon. I don't know whether Mr. Seselj is available on Monday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we might not need this time on Monday, but you never know. On the agenda for today I would like to address three main points respectively, A, the contempt procedure; B, the decision I handed down on the funding of the defence of the accused; C, the date of the trial. But before I look into these matters as Mr. Seselj is representing himself, I would like to tell him that the Plenary Assembly of the Tribunal has amended the Rules of Procedure and Evidence last July pertaining to Rules 62, 72, has deleted Rule 71 bis, has amended Rule 80 bis and Rule 75. I will give those documents to Mr. Seselj both in English and in French because the Rules of Procedure and Evidence are supplied in both languages, and there is no immediate version in B/C/S. Rule 62 does not concern you directly, Mr. Seselj, because this pertains to the initial appearance of an accused and relates to the issue of Defence counsel. Rule 72 relates to preliminary motions, but Rule 72 has not been amended in detail, with the exception that when the accused has no Defence counsel, the 30-day time limit only starts running once a Defence counsel has appointed -- or once he has indicated to the Registry pursuant to Rule 45 bis that he will represent himself. Rule 80 bis pertains to video-conferencing. This Rule entitles the Chamber ex officio to hold its hearing via video-conference. The next Rule has to do with witness protection when another jurisdiction is seized of the case. A particular procedure is then applied. Normally speaking, Mr. Seselj, you should have the translation of the Rules into B/C/S, but I don't believe that you have received the translation of these articles today. If you have received them, please let me know if you have received them please let me know if you haven't. In that case, I will give you a copy of the amended Rules in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure I remember what Rules exactly, but a week ago I did get the amendments to the Rules, so I assume that these are the ones that you've been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to check this with you. As far as the contempt procedure is concerned, the complaint you filed against the OTP, as you know the Trial Chamber has -- the Pre-Trial Chamber handed down a decision last July dismissing your application on re-examination of the initial decision issued by the Chamber. In brief what the Pre-Trial Chamber has decided runs as follows: The complaint you filed against Ms. Carla Del Ponte and her associates has not been dismissed because had it been dismissed we would have handed down a decision to that effect. I have decided as well as the two other Judges sitting on this Bench that the trial will rule -- the Trial Chamber will rule on the merits of your complaint once the Chamber has heard the various witnesses in question. The witnesses you mentioned in your complaint in which you stated that these witnesses had been pressured into providing a testimony. The advantage of such a procedure runs as follows: When these witnesses come to testify, whether they be Prosecution witnesses or your own witnesses, you will be able once they have taken the oath, to put questions to them directly on the way in which their statement was taken, because as you know, during cross-examination you are entitled to put questions relating to the credibility of a witness, and in that case, as these witnesses will have taken the oath, they will answer your questions. In addition, if there are any witnesses who are not called by the Prosecution, witnesses which figure on your list of witnesses, because you have provided us with such a witness list in that case as part of your Defence case you will call these witnesses to testify, and during the examination-in-chief you will then ask them under oath what actually happened when their statement -- statements were taken. And it is on the basis of the outcome of this that the Chamber will draw its conclusions. The other solution would have been to dismiss your complaint outright. This has not been adopted by the Trial Chamber. According to Rule 77, the Chamber could have appointed an amicus curiae who would have conducted an investigation, but in that case the witnesses could not have been heard under oath in the courtroom. The procedure that the Chamber has adopted protects your rights entirely and will entitle you, as you are representing yourself, to put questions to the witness. These witnesses will thus have to answer your questions, because if they do not they can be charged with contempt of court. And in addition, they will testify under oath, which is a different thing and is something different from testifying before a solicitor, a lawyer, or any other person. This is of greater value. This is why we feel that in this manner your rights are entirely protected. And if the truth should surface, the truth will surface in the presence of all the Judges who will have heard these witnesses. This is what I had to say on this particular matter, because the Chamber has not granted your application to review the initial decision that was taken. Do you wish to say anything about this, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I have already submitted a request to -- for certification to appeal that ruling of Chamber III. The question of principle is who are these contempt proceedings against, against me or members of the OTP? The Chief Prosecutor and her associate who acted in this case. As far as I know, not a single one of the 34 witnesses who gave depositions to me or, rather, to my associates are not Prosecution witnesses who are supposed to appear in the proceedings against me. Not a single one of these 34 witnesses. Secondly, when I call my own Defence witnesses and expert witnesses, I intend to challenge the positions of the Prosecution, and that is why I need to have equal time and an appropriate number of witnesses. As for my time, the time for the Defence case, I cannot use that to bring in witnesses who would accuse the Prosecution here and who would be quite indifferent as far as my defence is concerned. They would have to make statements as to what they were subjected to in terms of the unlawful behaviour of representatives of the OTP, and I have no questions to put to them within my own Defence case. Out of those 34, perhaps I plan to call one or two of them as Defence witnesses, but most of them I do not intend to call, and I do not have the scope for that kind of thing. Secondly, if this trial indeed begins in November, then roughly the Prosecution will be calling their witnesses by May or June. Among them there probably won't be any of the 34 persons in question because they refused to testify for the Prosecution. That's what they told me, all 34 of them. Then there is the three-month break like in all other trials, and that brings us to the month of September. If the trial really begins now in November or perhaps in August next year, then the Defence case would start. That is too long a period of time. Carla Del Ponte is leaving in September. If by some misfortune they extend her mandate until December, then she leaves in December. Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff has already run away from The Hague Tribunal. Now what happens to this third person that I brought charges against, I forget name right now, ah yes, Daniel Saxon, I don't know, but I see he's been removed from this case. So what is the point of contempt proceedings then? Contempt proceedings in principle are supposed to have priority over all other proceedings because that is the most serious thing that can happen in the functioning of this court which directly jeopardises the authority of this court and without that this court cannot bring justice, administer justice, even if this court had been founded legally, that is the way things would stand. In principle, until the factual basis is examined in these proceedings there is no point in doing anything else. These are proceedings that are supposed to be quite independent of the proceedings against me. So in two parallel courtrooms for that matter, if an amicus curiae is engaged or a special prosecutor or if the Trial Chamber act on this themselves. Last time and the other time before that you refer to all the options that you had available. So this doesn't hinder these proceedings in any way. There is a new OTP team here. As far as I know, I haven't brought charges yet against any one of the members of this team so that will not hinder their work in these proceedings in any way. As for those for whom I have proof that they committed the crime of contempt of Court they should be held accountable, or my complaint should be dismissed outright as untrue. It is my understanding that you did not dismiss it outright. You looked at the options that were the best for looking into it further. I don't think that this is a good option. I think that this should be treated urgently so that justice would prevail against those who committed contempt of court. Once Carla Del Ponte leaves it will be impossible for you to try her for contempt. Off she will go to Switzerland. As far as I know the UN is -- Switzerland is not a member of the UN - correct me if I'm wrong - and after that I hear she will be going to Argentina as ambassador. So she will be quite inaccessible and her closest associates probably will be too. So nothing doing. That is why I have dealt with it this way, certification to appeal and then I will file an appeal with the Appeals Chamber if you allow me to do so. If you do not allow me to do that, then do not count on me using my defence time to prove that OTP members committed the crime of contempt of Court. I have to use my time to refute the indictment. I'm not here to prosecute world justice. I'm not going to use my time in order to bring Carla Del Ponte behind bars. Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff and Daniel Saxon too. I came here to vanquish The Hague Tribunal, but how? By tearing apart the indictment brought against me. All the rest is of secondary importance. Even this thing, the complaint I filed, is of second rate importance from the point of view of my case that is, but is very important for this international court and for international justice in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us that you are going to apply for certification to appeal. The Chamber will rule on the certification of appeal which you will file. I cannot commit you anything here because this decision has to be taken by all the members of the Bench. One point of clarification I would like. The contempt of Court has not been filed against you. Maybe this is a translation problem. You wondered whether this these contempt proceedings concern you. No, you're the plaintiff against members of the OTP. You are not accused in this particular case or charged of contempt proceedings. Rest assured these proceedings do not concern you as an accused. Secondly, you stated that there are 34 witnesses, statements of which you have sent in. If these 34 witnesses come to testify here, you will be losing time. This is not a minor issue, because the witnesses could come to testify on the merits of the case. In purely technical terms, when the questions are put this is a very quick process. How was your statement taken? What were you told? Were promises made? And so on and so forth. This can be over in 15 minutes. Somebody can ask the essential questions which you will put to him or her. So I think there are no concerns about the time factor. I think you are concerned, however, about allocation of time. When the Prosecution, for instance, has 100 hours, the Defence then has 100 hours. You will have exactly the same time as the Prosecution. And secondly, if the Prosecution calls a hundred witnesses to testify, you are entitled to call a hundred witnesses to testify. This is what equality of arms is all about. So your concerns may seem subjective, but in practical terms rest assured, because you will not be prejudiced. You are applying for a certification of appeal. I don't know what my colleagues will think about this. We will hand down a decision on this particular application. Last point, which is an important point. You were saying that if the proceedings do not start now, Ms. Carla Del Ponte and the other people will vanish into thin air. That is not the case, because the Chamber can call a witness, including Ms. Carla Del Ponte, and if the witness does not come to testify the Chamber can issue an arrest warrant. So immunity does not apply here. If one day we feel it is important to hear those people whose names you have mentioned, they will be called whatever their future positions might be. There is no immunity here whatsoever. I shall now move on to the second item, which is an essential issue which pertains to the decision I handed down relating to the funding of your defence. During the summer recess, hour after hour, I kept abreast of the translation issues of a document of 20 pages. At the beginning of the afternoon I have been told that you have not received the translation of the decision I handed down in your language. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have received the decision. I received it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all the better then. So you have now got the decision in your own language. I shall briefly comment this will decision, because I realised that following this decision a number of comments were made in the Belgrade press and a number of legal "experts" who have commented this decision. These comments did not include or consider a number of fundamental rights of the accused. First of all, I would like to remind you that in this decision the right to represent yourself is a right that is enshrined in the Statute, a right which has been confirmed by the Appeals Chamber on two occasions. As far as the fact that you are representing yourself is concerned, these proceedings before this Tribunal is common law proceedings. In other words, the investigation which is conducted by the OTP is conducted by the OTP and the OTP only and is not monitored in any way by a Judge, whereas in the civil law system the Judges may monitor the investigation process. An investigation Judge can, for instance, be working together with a prosecutor or a magistrate. The Defence team then waits patiently for the outcome of the investigation before starting to prepare its case. In this case the Prosecution is solely responsible for the investigation, collects and gathers all evidence. The Defence then on the basis of the equality of arms can then call its own witnesses and own experts, to go and fetch the witnesses, and all this costs money. So given the procedure adopted here, the accused quite clearly has to incur a number of costs. All these costs have to be borne by the Tribunal. In addition, the statute has granted the accused a number of rights, and in the Statute - I think a lot of people have omitted to consider this - is the word "at least." So given the number of rights listed in the Statute, these rights may be supplemented if necessary. I feel that you have the right to defend yourself, and in order to do so you need to be provided with a team of people who will enable you to prepare your trial. The people assisting you need to be paid. This is the only way of guaranteeing a fair trial, because in a fair trial you are entitled to examine and have the Prosecution witnesses examined and call your own witnesses. For this right to be applied, you need to have enough resources available. This is what happens when an accused represents himself and when he needs to incur a number of costs. Some people feel that you should perhaps not those resources which would make it possible for you to adequately prepare your defence. The next point has to do with adducing evidence, and when you are preparing your evidence, and this is in the interest of the Bench, also your defence needs to be prepared in a consistent, efficient, and concise manner, and having to manage hundreds of documents, thousands of pages, statements and various documents calls for a team of people to help you to do this. It is not possible to deal with an avalanche of material on your own. This is why you need people to help you to do this. This decision has borne in mind the measures that need to be taken in this respect. These relate to two essential factors. Insofar as the costs are borne by the Tribunal, you should in that case be able to prove that you are not unable to cover those costs yourself. These costs could amount to tens of thousands of euros. I have reminded you of this in the decision. You should, and this is something you told us at the hearing and I have mentioned it in the decision, you should indicate to the Registry what your position is, and this is something you have mentioned on several occasions by providing documents in support of what you're saying. For instance, a tax return, the status of your wealth is certified by a solicitor or notary. This is something you have to establish with the Registry. I have no doubt about the matter. You should explain how you stand, what your position financially is. As you have described it, you -- your position would justify an application, and you should -- some of your costs should be borne by the Tribunal, but you need to prove this. A number of letters -- there has been a number of exchange of letters, but this is something that you have to see with the Registry. The second measure to be adopted here as I mentioned in the decision, I have said that among the associates you are working with, you do have a number of associates. One of them or several of them need to meet the requirements of Rule 45 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence pertaining to the required qualifications when Defence counsel are assigned. In other words, a knowledge of humanitarian law, international law, criminal law, a certain amount of experience, and so on and so forth. Given the track record of your associates, I believe you will have no difficulty in stating that at least one of your associates is able to meet the requirements of the Rules. With regard to the amounts concerned, it is not for me to tell whether it should be 10, 20, or 40.000 euros. This is something for the Registry to decide. But empirically and in order to reassure those who may entertain some fears, the costs incurred by your defence will be quite obviously less than the cost that would have arisen if you'd had a lawyer, a co-counsel, possibly an amicus curiae, with the entire teams, support teams. So if you then sum it all up, it would have been bound to be much more expensive than the cost that you will have to bear or that you will cause. But this is a matter for the Registry to see with you, to see how all this is going to be considered. Moreover, I said in the decision that it was for the Registry, under the Practice Direction and the payment scheme to pay the amounts granted as legal aid and to make sure that the money is used properly. So this is again a matter that should be dealt with by the Registry. In this decision which you received yesterday, I said that all this had to be done immediately. Immediately. I believe that the Registry was waiting for you to obtain the decision in your language in order to arrange a meeting with you as early as possible and to see how to implement all these provisions. Indeed, as I explained to you, your trial could not start yet because there were some problems, and in my view there was also another obstacle arising from two fundamental questions, the first questions being the disclosure of material in your own language, Prosecution material, and also exculpatory material. This is being sorted out. Indeed, during the summer recess the Prosecution sent me some binders, and I believe that if I got them, you must have got them too. Second obstacle, it had to do with the way your associates were going to be paid. So since this has been settled, we are now going to be able to deal with the third item, which is the commencement of trial, the date. I'm now going to give you the floor for comments on this issue ever funding.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I never in any way made any conditions on the beginning of the trial. I never conditioned it upon the beginning of financing of my defence by the Tribunal. I made of course these motions reckoning that I had the right to do so. But I never said that if it did not work, if it wasn't met, I would not defend myself. My only condition was disclosure in Serbian and on paper and the registration of my legal assistants, and of course guarantees of my legal right to represent myself without anyone's imposed interference. I never set out this issue in any other way. Of course I believe the decision you have issued will have great importance for the further development of international law. It is the first specific concrete decision of this kind in international law, although the way to guarantee the defence of an accused already exists, even in this Tribunal. Unfortunately, your decision will not be applicable, because you included a clause whereby one of my legal assistants has to meet the requirements of Rule 45 which regulates the assignment of counsel, and it says that, first of all, requirements set out in Rule 44 have to be met. None of my assistants will ever meet those requirements. My legal assistants do not have to meet the condition of being law professors at a university or having a law practice in another state. I consulted others on this issue. The Registry insisted that my legal assistants have to meet all of the requirements set out for counsel, Defence counsel, and I always claimed that legal assistants are not the same thing as counsel or, rather, vice versa. And legal assistants do not have to meet the same requirements. They just have to have a degree in law, and I have to trust them. In this clash with the Registry, I won in December last year, and on that occasion the Registry registered three of my legal assistants. A while ago, the Registrar wrote in one of the communications, and that set out the position of the Registry on the issue of financing, that under my pressure and because of my hunger strike they made the decision, otherwise they probably wouldn't have made it. Something to that effect. These legal assistants shall remain my legal assistants until the end of this process. There will be no change in that. My legal assistants do not have oral or written knowledge of either English or French, and they will never learn those languages. My legal assistants will never have proper membership in associations of lawyers capable to appear before foreign courts. First of all because they are not counsel, they're not lawyers, and they do not need to be members. And second, I simply prohibit them from becoming members of such associations because various criminal deals are taking place there, especially now that Mr. Karnavas is providing over that association. Mr. Karnavas who was involved in contraband and smuggling of oil and cigarettes in the former Yugoslavia, and he appeared and represented Mr. Blagojevic in Mr. Blagojevic's trial despite the express refusal of Mr. Blagojevic. Therefore I prohibit my assistants from joining that association. That association furthermore never dealt with any violations of the rights of their clients. Their only concern is how much money they're going to make before this court. And there are many lawyers who wrote more motions seeking money from the Registry than any motions concerning the defence of their counsel. My legal assistants will have nothing to do with these people. I have already proved that my legal assistants have no criminal record, have never been convicted, et cetera, and now under para (vi) of Rule 44 there is something where it says that in the conduct of their profession -- in the pursuit of their profession or otherwise, they have done nothing which is dishonest or otherwise discreditable to a counsel." My legal assistants so far have done their utmost on my instructions, my express instructions to disrupt the credibility of this court, of this Tribunal, and they will continue to do so. They will use all the documents they have and all the other evidence to diminish public confidence in the International Tribunal. And now let's move on to Rule 45, which in paragraph (i) accumulatively sets out all the requirements previously set out in Rule 44, adding some more, including under item (iv). They have indicated their availability and willingness to be assigned by the Tribunal to any person detained under the authority of the Tribunal lacking the means to remunerate counsel. My legal assistants will never allow the court or the Registry to assign them to any other person. They work exclusively for me, and they will never be assigned to anyone else. I appreciate your goodwill, Judge, and I believe your decision is of huge importance for the international law. It will be quoted many times before the ICC, before this Tribunal and other international courts. Regrettably, however, it won't be applicable in this trial. Within a certain time I will make a motion to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, before we move on to certification of appeal, I would like to meet your concerns. I have listened to you, and if you do not mind, we are going to look together at Rule 44. Unlike what you stated -- first of all, let us recall that you had given three names to the Registry, and those names had been accepted by the Registry. So I fail to see why once the Registry has accepted those names, they would no longer do it now because they had been accepted already. So first of all, take that into account. The three names you had mentioned had been taken into consideration by the Registry. So that's one major factor. And I fail to see why the Registry would change their minds. Secondly, as to the requirements of Rule 44, the said Article basically applies to an individual who is a counsel, a fully qualified lawyer. And as to the question of the language, unlike what you said, paragraph (B) allows for a waiver. You can have a situation where you have somebody who speaks neither French nor English and only speaks B/C/S, in which case the Registry can accept such an individual. So there is an exception there provided for under (B). Therefore, the issue of language is not one that might actually negate the decision. Also, as far as I know, your associates have never been punished anywhere, so the (iv) does not apply. They have not been convicted in a criminal trial. There is therefore no reason why they should not be able to assist you. As far as I know, your associates have never behaved improperly; therefore, 6 does not apply. They have not provided any false or misleading information; therefore the 7th provision also not applies -- won't apply, and all of the provisions of Rule 44 are no obstacles to the three people you had mentioned. There could be some controversy as to paragraph E because it's about somebody who again be a lawyer or be a professor of law or teach law in a university. We just need to interpret this in broad terms. Thinking that -- of the three names you'd mentioned to the Registry, there could be one who became a lawyer in Belgrade tomorrow, and that would settle the issue. So you're not worrying because you think that the Registry is going to put obstacles in your way while it was not the case when you mentioned those three's names. If there was ever an obstacle, you can always speak to me about this and that obstacle will be lifted, will be removed. So before you think of applying for certification of appeal, take time to think it over, to see with the Registry how this decision is going to be implemented. I remind you that this is the first decision in the history of international or national justice. So this is going to be remembered. Indeed, it is here mentioned for the first time and held for the first time that a self-represented accused has the right to have associates who are not fully-fledged lawyers. So before you apply for certification of appeal, do see the Registrar in order to settle these issues. I am convinced, I repeat that I am convinced that the Registry is really willing to do their utmost so that you may have your own associates to help you. Last time I told you, but we'll come back to this later, I had told you that as far as I was concerned, the way I saw things, but of course you are in no obligation to share my views, but as far as I could see, it is in your own interest. I thought it was useful for you to do so because I as a Judge have to make sure that I keep the right balance between Prosecution and Defence so that you not be put in a situation where you are disadvantaged, and this is where the role of the Judge is most important. Why? And you'll see that very soon, because when you have examination-in-chief by the Prosecution, they have documents, sometimes hundreds of them, that are submitted to a witness. They can be thousands of pages long, and you would be alone. Regardless of your excellent qualities as a lawyer, you will not be able to face all this. The OTP has been preparing for years. Of course you have new faces here so the teams have been renewed, but the basic groundwork has been done, and they will have no trouble in calling their witnesses, in examining them, and in submitting documents. The documents will be in English but also in B/C/S. So don't forget that the examination will be conducted in English, because that's the language used by the Prosecution. Of course everything will be translated, but you need to have then with you associates who can understand French and English and your language. That would be an additional asset for you. On the contrary, if you only have associates who know B/C/S, of course it can be done, but it might be a disadvantage for you, a handicap. That's why I told you last time that among the people who are going to assist you and who will be paid by the Tribunal it would be useful to have at least one who knows English. But of course if you don't want that, you're free to decide, but I thought it was in your interest to have somebody in your team who could use English. This is the reason for this provision in Rule 44, but there is a waiver because that same Rule says that at the request of the accused if it -- where the interests of justice so demand the Registrar may admit -- well, here in the text it says a counsel, but here we could have an associate who doesn't speak either of the two working languages of the Tribunal. So it can be done. So before you go into applications for certification of appeal, think it over, meet with the Registrar. All my contacts with the administration of this Tribunal are such that I do believe that there is no intention to harm you whatsoever. If I'd seen anything of the kind, I would certainly have stopped it. So see with the Registry how they plan to implement these provisions, and only if there's a problem, and anyway, you can always talk to me about it by way of a motion in order to sort it out. So this is what I wanted to convey to you, on the one hand to reassure you but also to emphasise that this decision is not fashioned for you alone Mr. Seselj. It was crafted in favour of somebody who represent themselves in the framework of a common law type of proceedings in which the Prosecutor carries out their own independent investigation under no supervision by a Judge and in which the Defence has to carry out its own investigation, its counter-investigation, and has to call their own witnesses and experts. All this costs money, costs that can be borne by an accused if they have the means, but the costs being enormous, in some cases they have to be borne by the Tribunal itself, and that was the very meaning, the very purpose of my decision. I do believe that in this matter you will face no problem at all. You have the floor, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, as you said, you have alleviated my concerns, and I am not going to ask for certification of an appeal, but I want to avail myself of this occasion to tell you that I'm going to appoint Zoran Krasic, one of my legal assistants, to be my chief legal assistant. He is not lawyer by profession, but you know that he has written 90 per cent of all my submissions and he is irreplaceable for my Defence team. There is no way anyone else could occupy that place. I cannot push him aside just because he is not a lawyer and give someone else the first place. I expect after that submission of the Registry that the Registrar will cause problems on this issue. Maybe my concerns are premature and unjustified. You have now persuaded me that they are premature and, therefore, I will abandon my intention to ask for certification of an appeal, but I'm not going to abandon the appointment of Zoran Krasic to be my main legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, with regard to Mr. Zoran Krasic, I mean, I don't have the privilege of knowing him, but I have read with great care all the work he has put into the motions. It's excellent work, and it would indeed be inconceivable that he would not assist you. Why the Registry -- I fail to see why the Registry should be opposed to this. If you tell the Registry that this Zoran Krasic is going to be your main legal assistant, I don't think he's been prosecuted or tried or anything, so on the basis of the work he's done already, he seems to have all the necessary skills, quite extensive skills indeed. So in my view there is no obstacle whatsoever to Mr. Zoran Krasic being your main or lead legal assistants. If there is any problem at all, just put it in a motion and I'll hand down a decision. You are absolutely right. He is a major person for you, and from what I've been able to read that he's written, yes, he's important for you. And if you did not have him, it might be a problem, a handicap, in which case the principle of equality of arms could be jeopardised. So this was in relation to this matter of financing. I wanted to take stock with you, because you see the good thing about a Status Conference is that it makes it possible to have an exchange of views and sometimes to put problems out of the way. I did not give you the floor, Ms. Dahl, because this issue of financing was not within the scope of the Prosecution as such. It is indeed a purely financial issue under the jurisdiction of the Registry. We'll be working until 7.00 p.m., therefore, I suggest that we have a short break. It's now 5.30. Let's have a 20-minute break, and we shall resume then to continue until 7.00 in order to deal with the other items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Status Conference is resuming. I would like to address with the Prosecution and Mr. Seselj the date of commencement of trial. I should like to refer to the previous Status Conference. At the previous Status Conference, Mr. Seselj, you told me at the time -- or you submitted a number of arguments stating that the trial could not commence before the month of March. You also made a legal argument which I should like to recall. You stipulated that the Security Council in its Resolution had indicated that the work of this Tribunal and the trials ongoing, the trials should come to an end in 2008, and you told me that this would be a problem because your trial could not finish in 2008, and this would have or trigger a number of consequences. I did not say anything at the time to allow myself enough time to think about it, because as you know, I am responsible for seizing the Chamber, saying that the status -- for the pre-trial phase is completed and that the trial can commence. I spent my summer recess thinking about the matter, and the outcome runs as follows: I believe that this trial should commence in November for the following reasons: A trial had started last year in November, then there was a hunger strike which interrupted the trial, and since that time eight months have elapsed, and we are now in the pre-trial phase. As a rule, as far as I know, trials have not been interrupted for any length of time. Usually when such a problem arises the trials resume fairly quickly. I also wondered what kind of -- how you could be prejudiced if the trial started in November in light of swathes of documents. I think it is fairly obvious that you have not read all the hundred or thousands or millions of pages that pertain to your case. I then reviewed the indictment, and I shall get back to this, and the list of witnesses provided by the Prosecution. I must tell you, Ms. Dahl, that I am not at all in agreement with the schedule that you have provided. This is a confidential schedule. I shall not quote any names because the hearing will remain in open session. Now, from what I understand from the submissions of the Prosecution, the Prosecution would like to call witnesses who are going to be talking about the responsibility of Mr. Seselj. The Prosecution would like to call these first. This is a fundamental issue. And then call the fact witnesses. This runs counter to any criminal case. Before addressing the issue of the liability of a particular person, you need to understand what the person is charged with, what the person is held responsible with, and for what reason, what the event, what has happened, in what sense is it a criminal act, and it's only after that that we can understand that the accused might be charged with a crime that was committed. I cannot agree with the order you have suggested. This would be pure heresy to my mind. If you call witnesses who will say, "He's responsible for this and that," when we have no knowledge of what has happened, what destruction has been taken place, devastation, looting, or what might have happened in a number of municipalities, this would be inconsistent. Furthermore, not withstanding this inconsistency the rights of the accused need to be abided by. We need to bear these in mind. Before Mr. Seselj can cross-examine the witnesses who will come to testify on his involvement in the JCE, joint criminal enterprise pursuant to Article 7.1 on the events that unfolded as far as planning was concerned, giving orders, and aiding and abetting. So it is important to understand what has happened on the ground. What has happened on the ground is something which you can highlight by addressing each point one by one. A, the crimes committed in Hrtkovci, then in Vukovar, then in Slavonia, in Western Slavonia, then in Bijeljina, Brko, and Bosanski Samac, and Zvornik, Novi Nevesinje, and Mostar, and the area of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction replace "instigated" instead of "aided and abetted."

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: This would be an advantage both for the Bench and for you, Mr. Seselj, because the witnesses would come before the Court and talk about what has happened in the area of Vukovar. And that is how we can answer the question what, what happened, and what is the accused charged with. After that, the following witnesses will come to say XYZ is held responsible for this and that, and Mr. Seselj. This would be a major advantage, because Mr. Seselj would then see that the Prosecution would be building a momentum. The -- his team can concentrate on factual issues, witnesses will come to talk about what has happened. "I was in my house. People came along. They burnt the house down," and so on and so forth. This is not going to prejudice the accused, because he can then cross-examine the witnesses. What will need to be highlighted is -- are the facts, the events. Mr. Seselj can then better prepare for what comes after that. As I have said on a number of occasions, your indictment is a rocket with three levels. On the first level is what has happened. Second level, those people who have committed the crimes, identification of the latter. And the third level pertains to the responsibility, the nexus between the perpetrators of the crimes and Mr. Seselj. And this over time will enable him, as he needs to prepare at length his defence, this will enable him to prepare it well. I understand what you are saying. If you start off straight away about witnesses -- with witnesses who are going to talk about his criminal responsibility, you will be putting him in a situation where he will run into difficulties. To my mind, he will not be able to prepare for it, even if he's been preparing it for five years. But during those five years, I have the feeling and the distinct feeling that a lot of time has been spent on the proceedings per se rather than on the merits of the case. For him to be in the best conditions possible, I think this is the way we need to proceed. You are going to respond by saying it is for the Prosecution to -- to meet the burden of proof, which is not quite right, because Rule 90(F) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence entitles the Judges to monitor the way in which the witnesses are being cross-examined, the way in which the evidence is being accused, as well as the order in which the witnesses come to testify. So what the Prosecution is saying, "We do what we feel like doing," I do not agree with this, because it is for the Judges and the Pre-Trial Judge to say how these witnesses will come to testify. And there are two reasons for this and two reasons why this has been clearly mentioned in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. A, to make sure that the cross-examination and presentation of evidence is efficient to establish the truth; and secondly, to avoid any waste of time. The truth I am after, the truth that my colleagues are after, is the truth with a capital "T", not the truth provided by the Prosecutor, not the truth provided by Mr. Seselj. In short, the truth. And the truth, so that there is no miscarriage of justice, needs to prevail. The order in which the witnesses are called needs to be consistent. It is very important in light of the fact that this is a difficult case, that there have been many ups and downs, that a person has been waiting now for five years to be tried, which is by any standards exceptional. As far as I'm concerned, this case presented no major difficulties. I think the time has come to stop wasting our time, and I put it to you that when the trial is going to start in November, the trial should start with witnesses who are going to come and talk about what has happened. After that, things will be stepped up. Mr. Seselj, I understand what your difficulties are and how difficult for you it is to manage your defence. It hasn't escaped me that a number of documents had not been disclosed to you, that a number of documents have not been translated, or that the translation is pending, and quite rightly so you can turn round and say, "Well, can I prepare my case?" As far as the crimes in question are concerned, yes, because the witnesses will come to talk about what has happened, and more often than not what they will talk about is public knowledge. You will then have the same time as the Prosecution has had with that witness to cross-examine him or her, and this should not pose any difficulty whatsoever. As far as the rest of the trial is concerned, if things start speeding up because a number of witnesses is much shorter or that there are fewer witnesses than expected and experience has shown that the Prosecution has a very long list of witnesses and that at the end of the day there are fewer witnesses, in that case we then need to switch to important witnesses either because we will be addressing the perpetrators of the crimes or because we shall be talking about your responsibility. You can then, if need be, ask the Chamber for a short suspension to enable you to prepare adequately. Suspension for a few weeks, which means that we can protect your rights entirely. But we need to start in November, because this has lasted long enough. At the end of the day, I don't know what the outcome would be, what your fate will be. This will be set according to the material adduced by the Prosecution, challenged by you, and also any material which you will provide. For the time being I have nothing. This will lead either to your acquittal or to a conviction, but as things stand today I don't know. It is only at the end, after assessing the evidence in light of its probative value and relevance, that the Bench will draw its conclusion. But for the time being my idea, contrary to what you think, because sometimes you give us the impression that you feel you have already been convicted, you have in front of you Judges who are wholly impartial and honest, who will assess the weight to be given to the evidence. They will hand down a decision either to acquit or to convict, but it is impossible to say today that you will convicted. Every time you say that as far as you're concerned you're going to be convicted, I will say no, Mr. Seselj, no, because a trial is an account over time. There is evidence and counter-evidence, and there is only -- it is only right at the end that we determine the matter. When I met you for the first time I told you trust this Tribunal, because this Tribunal has already handed down decisions. Some accused have been acquitted. Some accused have been convicted. This is not a Tribunal that convicts automatically. Let me remind all and everyone that the Judges must determine on the guilt or not of an accused beyond any reasonable doubt, which means that everything needs to be proven by the Prosecution on whom rests the burden of proof. The Defence, and that is what a fair trial is all about, and you yourself will be able to contradict the argument put forward by the Prosecution, or you will be entitled to cross-examine, to provide your own evidence, and it is in light of that that the Chamber will rule on the matter. I and my colleagues who are not here today, we have -- don't have any documents yet either from one party or the other. It is once these documents will be adduced, once this will be discussed, once the witnesses will start to testify that we will determine the matter, but for that to happen the trial needs to start. You should be able to defend yourself. You've already done so on a number of occasions. You will be assisted by people who seem to me to be fully competent, and the trial will not be a biased trial but a real trial, but for that to happen the trial must start. I think that if we start on the month -- in the month of November that is a good idea. In the first weeks of November the Prosecution will present its case. You might take the floor to challenge what the Prosecution has said, and the week after that we will start calling the fact witnesses who will come talk about what has happened. Mr. Seselj, you are going to turn round and say, "That's all very well, but what about the indictment, which I challenge?" And you're going say to me how can we start the trial when the indictment is being challenged. On this particular point which is an important point, I will answer by saying the following: You have filed a number of motions on the indictment, on the initial indictment, and on the amended indictment. The Pre-Trial Chamber, the Presiding Judge Robinson, Judge Bonomy, and I will determine the matter, and I hope that we will be able to rule on this before November. Of course after having ruled on the matter, you might not agree with the decision that has been taken, and in that case you may turn to the Appeals Chamber. But when an indictment is challenged, this does not mean that the trial cannot commence. In what way would this prejudice you? It does not prejudice you, because if you challenge the indictment, this does not mean that you will be further incriminated. Therefore, the decisions that will be taken will either be taken in your favour or will uphold the indictment. This, in any event, will not prejudice you further. In addition, and you know this as well as I do because you are a legal expert, you know as well as I do that the Rule provides for an amendment to the indictment at any time, even when the trial has already started. There are a number of examples that could be mentioned that the indictment has been amended after the trial has commenced. The fact that an indictment is not consolidated does not preclude this Tribunal from working and doing its job. Admittedly in civil law countries or systems like your country and mine, the cases start once the indictment has been consolidated and once the indictment is a definitive indictment, but in this case we are in a mixed system, and my predecessors have felt that amendments could be made to the indictment in the course of the trial. We are therefore in a different system. So as you come from a country, a civil law country, I understand your reaction perfectly well, but here the indictment can be amended at any time. And the Chamber will issue its decision before the beginning of the trial. After that, of course, the issue of filing an appeal is something different. The Prosecution or you might wish to seize the Appeals Chamber, but that is a different story. So the indictment is not a real problem, and at this stage I feel it is in your interest to start this trial and that the trial should start in November. You're going to tell me that I am an optimist, but we need optimism always. I know there are problems, obstacles. I know, for instance, that I don't even know the identity of the two Judges who are going to assist me. I don't even know the make-up of the legal officers of the Trial Chamber. As you know, so far I only had the assistance of one legal officer and an intern, and it was a very small team indeed, and still I'll manage to work on the pre-trial stage since the beginning the year. And as you can imagine, this has caused a lot of work for me and my associates. An easy solution would be to say, yes, let's quietly wait until March to start, but that would be a dereliction of duty on my part, because I see no obstacle to the trial being started, because I have removed these obstacles. I'll venture to say that this trial should have -- should have started when you surrendered to the Tribunal, in the six months that followed your arrival. There was no reason in my view why you had to wait all these months, all these years. Later on some may compare the initial indictment with the latest and may wonder why there was such a waste of time. I regret it very humbly at my level. I'm trying to catch up with lost time. This is the reason why I'm turning to the Prosecution. I tell them that they have to work, taking into account the specific circumstances and in trying not to do just whatever crosses their minds. The Prosecution has to adduce evidence pursuant to Rule 90(F) and in keeping with the instructions of the Chamber. Therefore, your document of the 25th of July can be approved by me in the (ii) the (iii) also, but I'm asking you to put the "i" right at the end, and I shall hand down a ruling to the effect. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, before you enter that order, although you mentioned what you considered to be the Prosecution's argument on the matter, I would like an opportunity to address you today on that issue. Regarding the order of witnesses, there are two points I would like to make. First, the gravamen of this case is Mr. Seselj's individual criminal responsibility, and we consider that the evidence from witnesses closest to him should come first. There does not appear to be a reasonable basis on which to contest many of the criminal episodes that form the basis of the indictment, namely, that because of their ethnicity people were killed or expelled from their homes, that men and women were raped and tortured, that places of worship and educational institutions were destroyed. The key evidence will be that linking Mr. Seselj to these events. The testimony -- The second point I want to make is that there are significant security risks associated with the testimony of witnesses for whom we have sought delayed disclosure and protective measures. It is incumbent to permit the Prosecution to present the evidence from these protected witnesses as soon as reasonably practical after the lifting of the measures protecting their identity. The more important and pressing question regarding the order of the Prosecution's case is the form of the evidence that the Chamber will hear. Will it be in written form or viva voce? The estimates provided by the Prosecution for the length of their case are based on reception of evidence primarily in written form. If the Chamber rejects those motions and favours the presentation of evidence orally and does not at the same time lengthen the time allowed to the Prosecution to present its case, then adjustments will have to be made. So I would consider that ruling on the motions for reception of evidence in written form should come first before the Chamber seeks to rearrange the order of the presentation of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, let me answer straight away. As to the security of witnesses, these witnesses have been waiting for five years and a few months -- or if you add on a few months is not going to change much basically to the issue of security risks. I fail to see how they would be less safe today than they were five years ago. That's my first comment. Second comment, and here you go to the merits of the case, which is of utmost interest to Mr. Seselj. It's bound to be for him. It is whether as a matter of fact or how the trial is going to unfold. I believe is that your starting point was that a large amount of the evidence will be adduced in writing. That's what you said. That's what you explained. And this is the reason why you filed many motions for admission already now of a series of evidence under 92 bis or under other Rules, starting with the testimony of Mr. Seselj in the Milosevic trial. I've already told you that I cannot commit myself on behalf of my colleagues, on behalf of the Trial Chamber. If I did so, that would be putting them before a fait accompli. One Chamber would have sovereignly decided that certain documents to be admitted, and as you know perfectly well, when a document is admitted it has some relevance, it has some probative value, whilst the accused would not be in a position to cross-examine the witnesses concerned, and at this stage of the proceedings could not present his views unless he files motions, and this is something I'm totally against at this stage of the proceedings. This is the reason why no decision has been made. I could issue a decision in the very next minutes or in the very next hours, but I decided not to. I decided not to take any decisions, because I wanted to refer these motions to the Trial Chamber, because the Trial Chamber is made up of three Judges, and I personally cannot replace my colleagues to say that this witness under -- is admitted under Rule 92 bis. Moreover, as I've already said to you, a trial is a construct, a piece of architecture. You have foundations, you have walls, and you have a roof. The foundations, what are they? They're going to be the first viva voce witnesses to testify. They will come to testify viva voce to explain what happened with regard to crimes, to perpetrators of the crimes, who's responsible for them, et cetera. These are the viva voce witnesses. Then you have the 92 ter witnesses. That is the situation when the Prosecution calls a witness, asks for the written statement to be admitted, puts a few questions to the witness, and then gives the witnesses to the Defence for cross-examination. Thereafter, you have 92 bis witnesses who come to corroborate things that the Judges have already heard. So let's not put the cart before the horses. Sorry for the metaphor, but I think it speaks for itself. Therefore, you have witnesses who come to testify viva voce. Then you complement this with 92 ter. Finally, you file a motion under 92 bis to explain that those witnesses should come in order to complete or to add on to this or that witness came to say to a certain point previously. Therefore, your approach, which is to think that this trial is going to be a trial in writing and that Mr. Seselj will not be able to say anything, well, I'm against it, because I'm not the Prosecution's toy. My mission is to deliver justice impartially by examining and assessing evidence. I hope you understood what I meant to say. And before I give you the floor, I'd like to say a final word. The Milosevic statement in the Milosevic trial, Mr. Seselj is in agreement. He is not opposed to it being admitted, but for Annex A. So you see, I know the file. But of course I could issue a decision straight away to admit it, but I want my colleagues to assess this, to look into this in order to decide whether indeed Mr. Seselj's testimony in the Milosevic trial, which he does claim to be good because in his filings, and I quote him there, he said, "I'm proud of it." And so on the basis of all this, I could easily make a decision, but I want this to be endorsed by my colleagues. This is the reason why I have not ruled, although Mr. Seselj is in agreement except for Annex A. Of course, Annex A is a source of problems, and those problems have to be dealt with by my colleagues too. The way you wish to approach this trial can be shared by me in part but not totally. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to perhaps point out a translation issue. I don't think it is the Prosecution's approach to have the trial completely in writing and to preclude Mr. Seselj from testing the evidence through cross-examination. Before you indicated that you were not interested in the Prosecution's of the version of the truth or Mr. Seselj's version of the truth but that you sought truth with a capital "T", and I submit that there are no separate experiences or varieties of truth, and what we seek here today is the same truth that the Chamber seeks. We do not consider the Chamber the Prosecution's toy, and I reject that characterisation of the role that we play in this case. I consider also that the order of presentation of witnesses is within the remit of the Prosecution to consider how best to offer its evidence in the most persuasive fashion and that it is of the same nature as the reception of evidence to be determined by the Chamber as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Dahl, I heard you, and I'm very pleased to know that you as well as I seek the truth with capital "T". Fine. And I'm sure that this goes for Mr. Seselj. Well, there is total consensus in this matter. However, there was one point I don't agree on with you. Rule 90 does not give the Prosecutor the freedom to do whatever they please. It is the responsibility of the Trial Chamber. It may be that this was not the rule generally applied in this Tribunal, but as far as I'm concerned and on the basis of my experience over several trials, I can tell you that it is incumbent on the Judge to say how the order of presentation of witnesses should be so that it shouldn't be confused or for nobody to understand what's happening. Some logics must be applied. Since you have taken over this case, I noted with great pleasure that you have made a very serious effort. I have no criticism to level there. However, with regard to the order of witnesses, it is a very important matter. So much so that, and this is another reminder, when the trial began the previous Trial Chamber said that you were entitled to call 102 witnesses, and you had 81 hours and 30 minutes to do so. In other words, other Judges before me held that it was the Trial Chamber who decided on the number of witnesses and on the time allocated for them. That's the general rule. I can refer you to recent case law by the Appeals Chamber, or in the other trial that I'm presiding over the Trial Chamber reduced the Prosecution time, which didn't please the Prosecution. The Prosecution appealed, but I was reaffirmed by the Appeals Chamber. This goes to show that the Judges can have the control of the proceedings. Secondly, following Trial Chamber I's decision of 8th of November, 2006, on the 27th of March, 2007, you set up a revised list of 105 witnesses. The Pre-Trial Chamber that I'm privileged to preside over, which has two associates, carried out an examination of the time needed for 105 witnesses, and if we total up the number of hours scheduled for these 105 witnesses, we conclude that you would need 269 hours, which is totally different from the 81 hours and 30 minutes imposed by the Trial Chamber, who was then presided over by Judge Orie. Now, 269 hours. You seem to say that out of these hours you have 92 bis and 92 ter witnesses. You must clarify this, madam. I need to know who you plan to call as viva voce witnesses, how much time you plan to devote to them in examination-in-chief. If I know that, I can say that if for a certain witness you had planned three hours, Mr. Seselj will also have three hours. Equality of arms is the principle. If for another witness you planned four hours, Mr. Seselj will also have four hours. He can decide not to use them, but he will have the same amount of time as you do. Let's speak about the viva voce witnesses -- or they were the viva voce witnesses. 92 bis witnesses. I need to know there, too, who the 92 ter witnesses are going to be. As part of them you may have 15 or 20 minutes to put this few ritual questions such as, "Are you the author of this written statement? Can you confirm it?" et cetera, and then you can adduce certain documents thereafter. The Trial Chamber will give Mr. Seselj a certain amount of time to this -- to the cross-examination of the 92 ter witness, but that is a time that is scheduled in the 65 ter list. Once all this has been done, the Trial Chamber will assess the overall amount of hours available to you in order to make your case. You've understood me straight away. This is within a bracket between -- of 81 hours and 269 hours. Yes, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The witness list we filed in March 2007 has all of the information you just described regarding the estimates of viva voce testimony and the time needed for witnesses who would be offering an abbreviated testimony supported by a written statement. I'm puzzled to come up with the 269 hours, and if we do reconvene on Monday, I'll do some homework to figure out perhaps where that came from, but I had studied the prior transcripts and the prior rulings and had reached the same number that you announced first, the 80 hours to a hundred hours was my recollection, but I don't have my worksheets here with me in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Dahl. Yes, you'll have to look at it again. Personally, I've already carried out a first estimate. Of course just by rule of thumb, because I don't have the documents, but I saw that you had catered for a large number of hours, and I thought this is overly optimistic as an estimate and that can be reduced. But this can be done in the next Status Conference when we'll go through that. But main problem is around the 92 bis issue. Why is it a problem? In his filings, Mr. Seselj is against the admission of 92 bis statements. Let me refer you to the numerous submissions made in this respect in a nutshell. I'll stand corrected by Mr. Seselj if I'm wrong, but he encapsulates in his filings that he is entitled to cross-examination of witnesses and he wants to exert this right by asking witnesses to be called to the hearing and not in writing. This is worth a discussion among fellow Judges, but as far as I can see, we have a solution already in the Rules. Inasmuch as it allows under 92 bis for written statements to be admitted when the latter is or are of a cumulative nature and that other witnesses are about to give or have given oral testimony of similar facts or relate to historical or political or military background or consist of a statistical analysis of the ethnic composition or concern the impact of crimes upon victims or relate to the character of the accused or relate to factors to be taken into account in determining sentence. But we're not there yet. In fact, the only problem for the Chamber is to know which these cumulative facts are, but in its great wisdom, the Rule says that there are factors mitigating against it when there is an overriding public interest in the evidence being presented orally. Because a party in this case, Mr. Seselj, is opposed to this, because he says and demonstrates that this evidence is not trustworthy, but he'll have to point to this, or else that there are other factors which make it appropriate for the witness to attend for cross-examination. In practice, and I'm saying this for Mr. Seselj's sake, in practice how do Judges proceed? They have 92 bis motions. You yourself, when your turn comes you may also file 92 bis motions. They're read by the Judges, and the Judges check that the contents of the statements is of a cumulative nature comes to support what other witnesses have said. Let's take a very simple example. Let us imagine that there is viva voce witness who comes to explain that in his village where he used to live his farm was destroyed, and he adds at that time that the surrounding farms have also been destroyed, viva voce. Now, you have a 92 bis witness. A neighbour of his comes to say the same, saying that his farm too was destroyed in that village. That's how 92 bis works. But in order to proceed in this way, you need to have some evidence on facts presented by a viva voce. So, Ms. Dahl, this is the reason why I can't Rule on all the 92 bis motions. Firstly, because I don't know what those witnesses would have said because I haven't heard them, and secondly because I don't know how my colleagues feel about this. They might have a different view than mine. They may then decide -- but they make a majority decision if I don't agree but there will be a majority decision, and this cannot be pre-empted by me. I know -- I know that there are Trial Chambers that have already ruled during the pre-stage trial on 92 bis motions. As you can imagine, I'm a specialist, and of course needless to say, I wondered whether this had been done before, and indeed in the Boskoski and Ljubicic case such decisions were made, but in the said case the Trial Chamber referred cases like that to national jurisdictions. In other cases the Judgement Chambers ruled on the matter. That is why the 92 bis Rule cannot be implemented at this stage. As far as Mr. Seselj's commission is concern, i.e., his right to cross-examine, of course you are entitled to this right, Mr. Seselj, but I'm sure you will understand that the Chamber is -- has the saving of time in mind. For instance, a witness comes and talks about a farm that has been destroyed and a 92 bis motion is filed to admit another document that -- or statement that says the same thing. Of course I will admit or grant the motion, because your cross-examination on the second witness will not provide any further information, because when the first witness comes to testify you will be able to cross-examine the person in question, and you can say, "How many farms were destroyed?" "The farm of my neighbour was destroyed," and the neighbour can then come and testify according to our 92 bis Rule. Mr. Seselj, experience has demonstrated that the Judges don't go in all directions. The Prosecution will file this motion, but the Judges will realise that the witness needs to be cross-examined, and then we will deny the motion and stipulate that the witness will be cross-examined. Let me remind you that the Judges are entitled to put questions to the witnesses. We are not in a hundred per cent common law trial where the Judges twiddle their fingers and do not take the floor. According to the Rules, the Judges are entitled to put questions to the witnesses, and as far as I'm concerned I never hesitate to put any questions to a witness. Therefore, in certain cases in 92 bis statements may call for the presence of the witness in the courtroom. Mr. Seselj, to sum up, I have read your various submissions relating to the 92 bis Rule. You have the right to cross-examine the witness, and this lies at the heart of the rights of the Defence and the Statute of this Tribunal. But if you are to cross-examine, yes, of course, when the witness is an important witness. When the witness will discuss the behaviour of one or other person. But as the Rules stipulate, if you are to cross-examine someone who is a 92 bis witness, who provides statistical data on the ethnic composition, you may disagree, of course, and with this kind of procedure you are entitled to say, "I disagree, and therefore I would like this witness to testify. I challenge what he says about the ethnic composition. He is making a mistake," and then you submit your argument, and the Trial Chamber, in light of such a challenge, may call the witness or ask the witness to come to testify. There are -- there is a difference of opinion here. Other witnesses will come to testify. The Prosecution will call its own witness to challenge this. Otherwise, we would have hundreds of witnesses every time, and that is not possible. There again I'm turning to Ms. Dahl. Experience has demonstrated, and my experience and this Tribunal has shown that when you choose your witnesses, call the important witnesses. It is for you to choose your witnesses and present them to the Chamber. They're important to you but important to establish the truth. Do not set aside some witnesses to call witnesses who will come to talk about things which are important to the witness himself or herself but to call witnesses who are important to establish the truth. This is -- lies at the heart of the trial. This is what underlies the burden of proof. And this is important because Mr. Seselj can then challenge what is being said. It is for the Chamber to strike the balance, to protect the interests of justice. Tonight at the end week we are not going to settle this issue. Mr. Seselj, next week we shall meet again on Monday afternoon. I will give you the floor so that you can respond to the issues I have addressed, to the issues that Ms. Dahl has addressed, and you will state your position and your feeling on these matters. My associate has just told me that the hearing will be held in this courtroom at a quarter past 2.00. Once we have addressed those matters, I shall then turn to some of the outstanding motions on the issue of disclosure of material, and I shall also address the issue of special defence. We need further clarification on these issues. Over the next few days and weeks I will come up against a very great difficulty, because all the courtrooms are overbooked. There are seven trials ongoing at this stage. I'm going to find it very difficult to find a day to convene a Status Conference. My associates have contacted the people in charge of scheduling. As soon as we have a slot, we shall be able to organise this Status Conference. I may have to issue an order on a Status Conference. If there are no slots available, I have two other possibilities. A, I would hold a Status Conference at 8.00 in the morning. Unfortunately, we will only have half an hour in that case, because we need to have a 30-minute interval between two cases to change over the tapes. So if need be, I could hold a Status Conference on Tuesday at 8.00, on Wednesday at 8.00, and Friday at 8.00. As far as I'm concerned, that is not a problem. I can hold a status conference at 10.00 p.m. until 4.00 in the morning if need be. I am accustomed to that. The problem is you need to come to the Tribunal. From what I understand, the Dutch police does not want to carry out the transport at certain times. We have problems with the interpreters timewise which means that we do have time restrictions, which is somewhat of an inconvenience, but for my part I am available. Next Monday I was to hold a hearing with a witness. That has been cancelled, so I seized this opportunity straight away and reconvened another Status Conference. It is now 7.00 p.m. I know that the interpreters are becoming restless. Ms. Dahl, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: A brief housekeeping matter for the court reporter. I wish to note a correction needed in the English transcript at page 25, line 7. The speaker is attributed to the Prosecution whereas in fact the Pre-Trial Judge was speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, this point of the agenda has been going on for an hour and 10 minutes. I would need at least 10 minutes to shed some light on the issues because until now I did not take part in the discussion. First of all, I had never any misgivings about the final outcome of this process. Moreover, I said on many occasions that I'm not really interested in it. What is important for me is to win in the eyes of the public. I have no reason to doubt your objectivity and fairness because so far you have not given me any reason to doubt you, but I do doubt the impartiality of this Court. I think it is anti-Serb in nature and too many Serbs have been condemned here for me to trust this court. I am aware that this is a historic process. Such a process has never ever been happening before in international law. That's why it's important for me to win. I have lived long enough. I am no longer interested in the judgement. What I'm interested in is the trace I will leave behind me. To be quite honest with you, I want to come out of this process with glory. That is my only concern. Second, I never asked for a postponement until March, never. I just made an estimate based on the status of this case that it will not be possible to begin before. It's more convenient, actually, for me to begin in November. Let me remind you of some statements of Refik Hodzic, the porte-parole of this Tribunal. In the Belgrade publication Pres [phoen], he said that it was my fault the trial had not begun yet and that I had asked for a postponement to March 2008. This is a blatant lie. He also said I asked for additional time to prepare for the beginning of the time. I never asked for additional time. I only pointed out objective problems caused by the Prosecution with their inactivity for the past five years. He says the trial would have begun in November last year, but it was my fault it didn't because I had begun a hunger strike. Only great suffering and trouble made me start that hunger strike. There are many other things that Refik Hodzic said and that were published on the 6th of August in the daily called Pres [phoen]. Therefore, I agreed that the trial starts in November. However, is everything ready for trial? You see, last year the crime base was taken out of the indictment for Western Slavonia, Bijeljina, Brcko, and many other places. It's no longer in the indictment, but it is still in the material. Is it out or not? I now see that it isn't. Maybe it is still in the indictment. Maybe the previous Trial Chamber made the confusion, because they said it should not be in the indictment, but it should in the crime base. Things should be coordinated. This is a problem created by the Prosecution. I believe that as the Pre-Trial Judge you could already decide on this. Either evidence will be presented in the crime base on all these places and then the old indictment should be back in place, or the new indictment should be revised and the evidence should be reviewed. Otherwise, my hands are tied in many ways. Now, with these written statements, in one of their submissions the OTP clearly made it known that they were going to try to present most of the evidence through written statements. The application of 92(F) is no longer possible. That Rule applied -- sorry, 89(F). That Rule applied earlier, because it's sui generis, and cases that fall under it are in species. Nothing can be led any longer under 89(F). Then the application of 92 bis, ter and quater cannot be the prevailing method of presenting evidence. If it is, I am not going to take part in this trial. I don't want to look at Zombie witnesses in this courtroom. Those statements are written by the Prosecution, not by witnesses. Sometimes witnesses don't even read what's in them. In Milosevic 42 witnesses claimed they didn't know what was in the statement that written in English which they don't speak. I think something like that is impermissible. Then in the submission of the OTP which was given me on the 14th of July -- sorry, dated 14th of June and given me later, it's a motion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In footnote 28 on page 6 it says, I quote: "If the Prosecution is required to print out all the material that the accused has so far rejected, estimated at 400.000 pages, the costs of work and material resources would be higher than 75.000 euros." And in what time will they do this? So far they have presented me in some 50 binders around 10.000 documents, maybe more, I haven't been able to count. What about the other 390.000? When will that be served on me? It has to be served me before the beginning of the trial. There is enough documents that the Prosecution accidentally comes across when the trial has already begun. This is material that the OTP already had in 2003. They were just not ready to present them to me. That's the problem. How can you solve it. If you can solve it before November, I'm certainly not going to make a problem. I'm looking forward to it. I'm actually impatient. I have already found myself in this role, and I'm frankly looking forward to the trial. On the 25th of June the OTP gave me 35 witness statements under the decision of the Trial Chamber of the 4th of July and 16th May. Only two of them were in Serbian. The rest was in English, and I returned them. After your decision everything has to be in Serbian and on paper they keep persisting on -- on giving me material in English. Then the material on Vuk Draskovic and his Serbian guard whose crimes were ascribed to me in Herzegovina. Then the statement of a certain Ibrahim Sutar [phoen] is in English. He's not a protected witness, that's why I'm mentioning his name, what am I going to do with his statement in English? Then there is no system in the submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... You are quoting names. I don't know whether these are protected witnesses or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have checked. He's not protected, otherwise I would not have mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour in accordance with the suggestion I made at the last Status Conference, if names are mentioned the entire proceedings should be placed into private session so as to avoid inadvertent disclosure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be able to avoid -- [overlapping speakers] I'll mention this one in the certainty that he's not a protected witness. Then there is the question of relevance of the documents that are being presented to me. The OTP announced about 4.000 pieces of evidence, exhibits. So far 1 through 500 have been presented to me. Now, the question comes up of the relevance of this material. Do you know what they presented to me? Registries of births, deaths in Hrtkovci from 1945 through 2000. They are presenting me with the textbooks of the Command Staff Academy of the army of Yugoslavia, rules of corps, and rules of brigade. They are giving me textbooks of the military academy of ground forces, the strategy of armed conflict, the Statutes of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. They have 4.000 exhibits. Maybe 10 per cent are relevant. The rest are not. I'm drawing your attention that I will not allow a single exhibit to be admitted into evidence before the OTP demonstrates here that they are really relevant. It's their obligation under the Rules of Procedure. Many lawyers in many cases fail to pay attention to this. They think it has nothing to do with their witness so let it go into evidence. In this case, in my case, this will not work. They will have to prove that this is relevant for a reason. This textbook from the Command Staff Academy may be relevant in some way or the rule of corps, maybe I was the commander of a corps, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we're going to stop now because one is pulling my ears. It is 7.00 and we have exceeded our time. I shall give you the floor again on Monday. But between now and Monday, Ms. Dahl, I would like you to respond to a number of issues raised by Mr. Seselj at this very moment. So please read the transcript again, and I shall give you the floor so that you can respond to Mr. Seselj. I would have liked to pursue this hearing. It is it of great interest to me, but for a number of reasons we need to adjourn now. We shall meet again on Monday, and I wish you a pleasant weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: at 7.11 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
